# Afterburner

> One sandboxed, deterministic WebAssembly runtime for every language. Run or compile JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust, C and C++ to a self-contained wasm artifact with zero setup.

Afterburner ships as `burn`, a single CLI binary. It runs a script directly
(`burn run script.py`) or compiles a package to a portable `.afb` artifact
(`burn compile ./pkg -o demo.afb`). Every guest runs in a capability-sandboxed,
deterministic wasm environment with fuel-metered execution. It is also usable as
a Rust library via the `afterburner` crate.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://afterburner.sh | sh` (Linux and macOS), or
`iwr -useb https://afterburner.sh | iex` (Windows PowerShell).

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://afterburner.sh/docs#introduction): what Afterburner is and the problem it solves
- [Installation](https://afterburner.sh/docs#installation): install the `burn` CLI on Linux, macOS and Windows
- [Running scripts](https://afterburner.sh/docs#run): execute a script in the sandbox by file extension
- [First package](https://afterburner.sh/docs#first-package): scaffold and build a `.afb` package
- [Compiling](https://afterburner.sh/docs#compile): compile a package to a self-contained wasm artifact
- [Languages](https://afterburner.sh/docs#languages): the supported guest languages and how each is run
- [Determinism](https://afterburner.sh/docs#determinism): reproducible execution and the effect log
- [Sandbox](https://afterburner.sh/docs#sandbox): the capability model and what a guest can reach
- [Fuel](https://afterburner.sh/docs#fuel): metered execution and resource limits
- [Programmatic use](https://afterburner.sh/docs#programmatic): embedding Afterburner as a Rust library
- [CLI reference](https://afterburner.sh/docs#cli): every `burn` subcommand and flag

## Optional

- [REPL](https://afterburner.sh/docs#repl): the interactive shell
- [Execution tiers](https://afterburner.sh/docs#tiers): interpreter and compiled tier selection
- [Scheduler](https://afterburner.sh/docs#scheduler): the thrust work-stealing scheduler
- [State](https://afterburner.sh/docs#state): sharing state across invocations
- [Packages](https://afterburner.sh/docs#packages): the `.afb` package format and registry
- [Extending](https://afterburner.sh/docs#extend): host imports and custom capabilities
- [AI agents](https://afterburner.sh/docs#ai-agents): running agent-generated code safely
- [Node compatibility](https://afterburner.sh/docs#node-compat): supported Node built-ins and shims
- [Environment](https://afterburner.sh/docs#env): environment variables and configuration
- [Crates](https://afterburner.sh/docs#crates): the published Rust crates
- [Building from source](https://afterburner.sh/docs#build): toolchain requirements and build steps
- [Source repository](https://github.com/afterburner-sh/afterburner): issues, releases and source
